schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID,P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT AS P WHERE P.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT S.PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES AS S WHERE S.SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31')
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID,P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT AS P WHERE P.PRODUCT_ID NOT IN (SELECT S.PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES AS S WHERE S.SALE_DATE NOT BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31')
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects products whose all sales occurred within a specific date range (Jan 1, 2019 to Mar 31, 2019), whereas Q2 selects products that have at least one sale within that range, excluding products with any sale outside of it. This difference leads to different results when a product has both sales inside and outside the date range.
counterexample_dsp: A product with sales on both '2019-01-15' and '2019-04-01'. Q1 excludes it because not all sales are within the range, but Q2 includes it because it has at least one sale within the range.
